forecasts.reason: EMA/Lookahead gain at about 10 epochs is probably +0.0-0.1 pp, inside the roughly 0.1-0.2 pp noise. It adds a small cost for the extra kernels.
The same recipe should reproduce within about 1-3% in time and about 0.1-0.2 pp in accuracy. E003 shows 0.09 pp of drift on identical math.

cruxes: Why was torch.compile 1.5 s slower (12.07 s vs 10.55 s)? If compile or autotune cost leaks into the timed region, I006 improves, but only toward parity with eager.
Is the true accuracy slope about 0.65 pp per epoch at 10 epochs? If it is, 0.753 needs about 10.5-11 epochs, and no systems tweak changes feasibility.
How large is the 3-seed run-to-run accuracy noise (about 0.1-0.2 pp)? It decides whether EMA-sized gains are detectable.
structured_output.world_model:
E001 (9 epochs): acc 0.7430, time 9.43 s. E002 (10 epochs): acc 0.7495, time 10.55 s. E003 (compiled, same math): acc 0.7486, time 12.07 s. The best feasible recipe is still none; E002 is 0.35 pp short of 0.753.

Beliefs:
1. Epochs dominate time (H1). About 1.1 s per epoch, with a fixed cost of about 0-0.5 s. The accuracy slope is about 0.65 pp per epoch from 9 to 10, and I expect it to flatten. Reaching 0.753 therefore needs about 10.5-11 epochs, or +0.4 pp from elsewhere, which means a time of about 11.5-12 s. Support: E001 and E002.
2. Compile missed (E003). I predicted a 7-15% saving and measured a 14% loss. The most likely cause is compile, autotune or recompile cost leaking into timed prepare/train, or a ragged-batch shape. Eager is already compute-bound at batch 1024 with fp16 and channels_last. The lesson is that systems tweaks need explicit evidence, so I shade H2.2 claims down. Accuracy differed by -0.09 pp from E002 on the same math, which is a direct noise sample.
3. Noise. The per-seed accuracy std is about 0.3 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15 pp. Fixed seeds correlate the repeat runs, and cudnn nondeterminism adds a mean drift of about 0.1 pp. Time noise is about 1-3%. Any accuracy change under 0.2 pp is indistinguishable from noise.
4. EMA/Lookahead near 10 epochs is likely +0.0-0.1 pp, which is neutral. It costs a little time.
5. Muon is untuned at batch 2000, so I expect it to lose accuracy. Progressive resizing is likely to lose 0.5-1.5 pp for a 15-20% time saving, so it is not feasible on its own.
6. Regression. Small gains from lucky seeds regress, so I shade claims downward. The 40-seed mean is probably 0.1-0.2 pp below the 3-seed mean.

Unsure: the cause of the compile slowdown, the true fixed-cost share, and the flattening of the accuracy-vs-epoch slope.
